variant.stem_override: Fetal echocardiography by maternal-fetal medicine at 18 weeks of gestation demonstrates a fetal heart rate of 90 bpm with a 2:1 atrioventricular conduction pattern consistent with INCOMPLETE (second-degree, Mobitz-II-like) atrioventricular block — first detection in this pregnancy. There are no structural cardiac defects, no fetal hydrops, and the fetal anatomy is otherwise normal. The amniotic-fluid volume is normal. Two weeks prior, the PR interval was prolonged on fetal Doppler. Maternal vital signs are normal; she is asymptomatic. The patient is a 30-year-old woman in her first pregnancy presenting for routine fetal cardiac surveillance. She has known systemic lupus erythematosus with strongly positive anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies since her SLE diagnosis 4 years ago. She has been on hydroxychloroquine 400 mg/d throughout pregnancy.
variant.rationale_for_variant: The presentation now leads with the fetal echocardiographic and Doppler findings, then maternal examination findings, and finally the obstetric and rheumatologic history, reversing the conventional history-first order. All facts, numbers, and clinical details are preserved exactly; only their sequence has changed. The correct answer remains B because the clinical scenario — incomplete fetal AV block at 18 weeks in an anti-Ro/SSA-positive mother already on hydroxychloroquine — is identical and still represents an actionable window for maternal fluorinated corticosteroid therapy.
